newsitem.title: USA: NASD, MSRB mum on new board guidance on rule G-37.
newsitem.headline: NASD, MSRB mum on new board guidance on rule G-37.

text.p: National Association of Securities Dealers received additional guidance from MSRB on how to enforce "pay-to-play" rule G-37, but NASD is not making details public, a spokesman for the group said.
"There's nothing to report but that we've received the document and are considering all recommendations," Reid Walker, associate director for media relations, told Reuters.
Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board sent broad guidelines to NASD in June 1995 on how to enforce rule G-37.
The two-and-a-half-year-old rule bars municipal bond dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
But Mary Schapiro, president of NASD's new regulatory authority, NASD Regulation, Inc., said in a recent interview that the guidelines are not specific enough.
She added that until more detailed instructions are available from MSRB, NASD will take a hard-line stance on granting exemptions under the rule.
NASD will only grant exemptions, Schapiro said, under two narrow circumstances that were outlined clearly by MSRB in the June 1995 letter.
They are when a disgruntled employee deliberately makes a political contribution to trigger the two-year ban on business or when an employee inadvertently gives just over the $250.
Christopher Taylor, executive director of the MSRB, would not comment on the MSRB's recent letter to NASD.
Securities and Exchange Commission Aug 8 issued a report slamming NASD for failing to adequately enforce rule G-37.

Less than one month later, Theresa Carr, a former senior compliance examiner in NASD's district 10 office in New York City, filed a $20 million discrimination case against the association for blocking her efforts to aggressively probe pay-to-play in the muni market.
An association spokesman last week called the charges "meritless" and said NASD will vigorously fight them.

John Pinto, executive vice president of NASD Regulation, announced on August 16 that the association settled charges involving rule G-37 reporting requirements with 11 firms, including Salomon Brothers Inc and Morgan Keegan & Co.
Under the settlements, firms have agreed to pay $20,000 in penalities, Pinto said.
He said another 13 draft settlements totaling $38,700 in possible fines have been cleared by district NASD panels and are awaiting national action.
Meanwhile, NASD announced May 31 it plans to hire a "senior level person" soon to oversee the group's municipal bond compliance program.
And Schapiro, a former SEC commissioner, said on May 16 that NASD will create a separate tracking system that will make it easier for investors to identify firms that have violated rule G-37.
